- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1.00 to -1.00), model fails to adjust quickly; apply 1–3 day lag correction to forecast slope.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model overestimates bullishness; cap forecast growth at 0.5–1.0% per day unless sentiment confirms strong bullishness.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from forecast mean, check sentiment history for recent reversal signals; if present, apply mean reversion rule: forecast = prior 5-day avg + 10% of deviation.
